chunk_findings.detail: The option comparison collapses the tree’s option entries to a set of flag strings (`offered = {f for o in node["options"] for f in o["flags"]}`), so it does not enforce one option entry per parser action. If `T.command_tree` regressed to emit two identical entries for `--mode` (for example, one inherited global copy and one local copy), `offered == expected` still passes because the set is unchanged, and the per-option loop passes for each duplicate because both entries’ first flag resolves to the same argparse action and their flag list equals that action’s option strings. Thus the test’s “nothing extra” assertion accepts duplicate option objects in the tree.

chunk_findings.detail: The shell syntax test’s only semantic guard is `assert f"_ddflow_activate_{shell}" in text`, so a degenerate template can pass even though it does not define the activation function. For example, if `scripts.for_shell("bash")` regressed to return `# _ddflow_activate_bash` (or `echo _ddflow_activate_bash`), `bash -n` exits 0 and the substring assertion passes, yet the shipped completion script has no real `_ddflow_activate_bash` function. This contradicts the test’s stated intent to reject an empty/comment-only placeholder and lets a broken activation template pass the shell contract.
